'''Gautier Hamel de Monchenault''' (born 1964 in Paris, France) is a French particle physicist who has contributed to the [[Standard Model]], [[CP violation]] and the discovery of the [[Higgs boson]]. He is a senior researcher at the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]] (CEA).<ref>[http://www-centre-saclay.cea.fr/fr/fr/La-recherche/Portraits-de-chercheurs/Hamel-de-Monchenault Portrait sur le site du CEA]</ref> Hamel de Monchenault  is appointed CERN Director for Research and Computing for the period 2026–2030.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2025-06-23 |title=CERN management structure for 2026–2030, part 2 |url=https://home.cern/news/opinion/cern/cern-management-structure-2026-2030-part-2 |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=CERN |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Gautier Hamel de Monchenault graduated from [[ESPCI Paris|ESPCI ParisTech]].<ref name=":0">[http://www.espci.org/fr/anciens/eleves/102/ Ingénieurs de la de la 102ème promotion de l'EPSI]</ref>  He completed his doctoral research at the [[University of Paris VI]] and CERN, focusing on high-energy particle physics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hamel de Monchenault |first=Gautier |title=Etude de la résolution de la TPC de DELPHI: Recherche du boson de Higgs du Modèle Standard Minimal dans l'expérience Delphi |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/887272 |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref>

== Career ==
=== DELPHI experiment ===
Hamel de Monchenault began his research career at CERN as part of the [[DELPHI experiment]] at the [[Large Electron–Positron Collider|Large Electron-Positron Collider]] (LEP). He was involved in studies related to the Higgs boson and contributed to various physics analyses, including jet fragmentation functions and two-photon physics.{{Cn|date=June 2025}}

=== BABAR and CP violation ===
In 1992, he joined the [[BABAR collaboration]] at [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]], associated with the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory#PEP-II|PEP-II electron-positron collider]]. There, he played a pivotal role in the design and construction of the DIRC particle identification system.{{Cn|date=June 2025}} As a visiting scientist at [[Berkeley Lab]] from 1996 to 1998, he contributed to the simulation, reconstruction, and physics analysis software.{{Cn|date=June 2025}} From 1999 to 2001, he served as the Physics Analysis Coordinator for BABAR<ref name=":1">[https://www.nytimes.com/2001/07/07/us/tiny-discovery-may-answer-a-question-about-the-big-bang.html ''Tiny Discovery May Answer a Question About the Big Bang''] dans ''[[The New York Times]]'' du 7 juillet 2001.</ref> during the observation of CP violation in the B-meson system, validating the theoretical predictions of [[Makoto Kobayashi]] and [[Toshihide Maskawa]], who were awarded the 2008 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] for their work.

=== CMS and Higgs boson discovery ===
Hamel de Monchenault joined the [[Compact Muon Solenoid Experiment|Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment]] at CERN in 1995. He has held various leadership roles within CMS, including Deputy Physics Coordinator and Deputy Spokesperson. His contributions were instrumental in the discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012. He has also been involved in the design and operation of the muon detection system and has contributed to the electromagnetic calorimeter (ECAL).{{Cn|date=June 2025}}

=== Leadership positions ===
From 2016 to 2020, Hamel de Monchenault served as the head of the Particle Physics Department at [[CEA-Irfu]].{{Cn|date=June 2025}} 

In 2024, he was elected as the Spokesperson for the CMS collaboration, becoming the first scientist from CEA to lead one of the four major LHC experiments. His leadership coincides with the transition to the [[HL-LHC|High Luminosity phase of the LHC]], a period marked by significant upgrades to the detector and the continuation of pivotal physics analyses.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CMS Welcomes New Management for 2024-2026 {{!}} CMS Experiment |url=https://cms.cern/news/cms-welcomes-new-management-2024-2026 |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=cms.cern}}</ref>

Hamel de Monchenault  will serve as CERN Director for Research and Computing for the period 2026–2030.<ref name=":2" />

== Distinctions ==
Gautier Hamel de Monchenault is the recipient of the [[Prix Joliot-Curie]] from the [[French Physical Society]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-15 |title=Prix Joliot-Curie |url=https://www.sfphysique.fr/prix/prix-joliot-curie/ |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=Société Française de Physique |language=fr-FR}}</ref>
